full_judgment:
Farah Mahbub J : In this Rule, issued under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, the respondents have been called upon to show cause as to why the impugned Order dated 25-7-2010 passed by the Artha Rin Adalat, Bogra in Artha Execution Case No.170 of 2008 allowing the prayer of the decree holder bank making demand to pay 50% interest and legal charge, in total Taka 3,33,125,37 from the petitioner (Annexure-D) should not be declared to have been passed without any lawful authority and hence, is of no legal effect. 

 2. Facts, in brief, are that petitioner took cash credit facility (hypo) amounting to Tk 5,00,000 (Taka Five lakh) from Eastern Bank Ltd. Bogra Branch, respondent No.3 to meet the working capital in order to have smooth running of his business of selling and supply of various types of food grain. As per the requirement condition stocks of various types of food grain e.g. rice, paddy, wheat, pulses etc, were stored/ to be stored in the borrower's shop/godown which had been duly insured in the joint names of the respective bank and the borrower, covering the risks of Fire, and RSD and that minimum margin on stocks should be 30%. Subsequently, the respondent bank sanctioned another Taka 15,00,000 (Taka fifteen lakh) in favour of the petitioner which was disbursed on 13-2-2003 in his favour. The petitioner later on paid off Taka 7,00,000 (Taka seven lakh) on 15-5-2003. Meanwhile, having sustained heavy loss in business he filed an application to respondent No. 3 on 25-2-2004 for waiving interest and to re-schedule the defaulted loan amount. The respondent bank vide office letter dated 3-6-2004 rejected the said prayer without any cogent reason and to recover the defaulted loan amount had instituted Artha Rin suit No. 11 of 2007 for Tk 25,18,741.94 with interest by selling the mortgage property in auction. The petitioner contested the suit by filling written statement. After conclusion of trial the Artha Rin Adalat, Bogra decreed the suit on contest vide judgment and decree dated 25-3-2008 (Annexure A and A-1) finding, inter-alia, 

 3. Accordingly, the decree holder Bank made an application before the executing Adalat for execution of decree demanding Taka 25,34,323.02 in total (Annexure-B). Meanwhile, the petitioner upon obtaining permission from the executing Adalat had sold out the mortgaged property as described in "Kha" schedule of the execution case and paid the total decretal amount to the decree holder Bank through the Adalat. To that effect the petitioner also made an application before the Adalat on 22-4-2010 with documents about the payment of the decretal amount and made a prayer to return all the original deeds and documents including the mortgage deed to the petitioner (Annexure-C and C1 respectively). It has been contended that the respondent bank had demanded legal charge of Taka 83,332, though earlier Taka 28,900 had been paid by the petitioner under the said heading. The Adalat without considering the fact that decretal amount had been satisfied by making payment to that effect passed the impugned Order dated 25-7-2010 directing the petitioner to pay further 50% as interest and legal charge, (Annexure-D) hence, the application. 4. Respondent Bank has entered appearance by filing affidavit-in-opposition contending, inter-alia, that the Artha Rin suit was originally decreed for Taka 22,18,741.94 after adjustment of Taka 3,00,000 (which was paid two installments on 5-8-2007 and 25-2-2008 respectively during the pendency of the suit from the claimed amount of Taka 25,18,741.94. On 4-5-2008 the respondent Nos. 2-3 bank filed Artha Execution Case No. 170 of 2008 for an amount of Taka 25,34,323.02 and amongst others had charged simple interest @ 12% PA on the decretal amount of Taka 22,18,741.94 up to 3-5-2008.  8. It is further stated that after making the payment of Taka 22,34,323.02 towards satisfaction of the decretal amount, the petitioner on 4-4-2010 submitted an application to the respondent Nos. 2-3 for waiver of the entire post decretal interest. The respondent Nos. 2-3 upon consideration of the said application waived 50% of the post decretal interest vide sanction letter No. LR/MR/1436 dated 17-6-2010 (Annexure-"1" and "1(a)" respectively). The respondent bank duly filed copy of the said sanction letter dated 17-6-2010 before the Executing Adalat by "firisti" and claimed the outstanding amount upon adjustment of the waived interest of 50% to the tune of Taka 2,49,793.65. On perusal of the same the Executing Court passed the impugned Order dated 25-7-2010 directing the petitioner to pay the balance amount on 29-8-2010. It is further contended that the legal expense of Taka 28,900 as claimed in the application of Artha Execution Case No.170 of 2010 pertains to the Artha Rin Suit No. 11 of 2007 and that the said amount had never been paid by the petitioner, whereas the amount of Taka 83,323.00 as claimed in the sanction letter dated 17-6-2010 is related to the legal charge at the execution stage (Artha Execution Case No. 170 of 2008) including publication of notices in the "Daily News Paper" etc. It is further stated that the petitioner did not pay the legal charge pertaining to the Artha Execution Case No. 170 of 2008, nor paid the pendentelite interest of the original suit or the interest for the post decretal period, in other words, after the suit being decreed the petitioner did not pay any other amount, except Taka 22,34,323.02. 

 9. Mrs Saleha Islam the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that according to the judgment and decree dated 25-3-2008 there is no scope to impose further interest to the petitioner, the relevant portion of the judgment and decree is as follows:— 

 11. On the other hand, Mr AZM Mohiuddin the learned Advocate for the respondent Bank goes to submit that sub section (2) of section 50 of the Ain, 2003, has duly authorised charging pendentelite interest and the interest for the post decretal period. Consequently, while passing the decree, the Adalat may not require to give any direction regarding the payment of pendentelite interest and the interest for the post decretal period till realization of the decretal amount, as those are covered by the statute itself. He further submits that as per sub-section (1) of section 50 of the Ain, 2003, the Artha Rin Adalat has no jurisdiction to waive any interest and therefore, the Executing Adalat has rightly passed the impugned Order dated 25-7-2010 in accordance with the said provision of law. 

 13. In view of sub-section (1) of section 50 the Adalat has no jurisdiction to waive interest from the date of disbursement of loan till institution of the Artha Rin suit. In sub-section (2) it has been provided that from the date of filing of the suit till realization of the decretal amount simple interest at certain rate, shall be imposed on the decretal amount for having used the word হইবে". In view of the said statutory provision particularly sub-section (2) direction with regard to the payment of interest for the period, from the date of filing of the suit till realization of the decretal amount, shall ipso facto be operative with the passing of the judgment and decree. Since law shall prevail unless being struck down as ultra vires the Constitution as such non-recording of any direction regarding payment of interest from the date of filing of the suit till realization of the decretal amount in the judgment and decree by the Artha Rin Adalat does not go the affect the right of the decree holder for charging the payment of interest as provided under section 50 of the Ain. In that view of the matter the Executing Adalat has committed no illegality while passing the impugned Order dated 25-7-2010 in Artha Execution Case No. 170 of 2008. 

 14. However, waiving the interest so accrued upon the decretal amount is the absolute discretion of the bank concern. The petitioner in his bona fide concern has paid the decretal amount as it was on the date of passing the judgment and decree on 28-3-2008. Considering the financial hardship of the petitioner the respondent-bank in it's own discretion may consider in waiving the said balance 50% interest as claimed before the executing Adalat.
